podcast.body: Released in 1982 as one of Madonna's first two singles, preceding her debut album. While generally commercial and unprovocative, its B-side video, featuring physical attraction, possibly contained the first hints of Madonna's future explicit and provocative style. "Posiblemente sí que ya tenemos los primeros trazos en lo que sería Madonna."

One of Madonna's earliest singles, released in 1983, it is described as "hard to pigeonhole" – a club record featuring prominent rock guitar. Inspired by her years in New York City punk clubs, the song possessed a sinister edge that sounded less like disco and more like post-punk or new wave. A quarter-century later, Blender Magazine ranked "Burning Up" as one of its "40 quintessential new wave songs." Due to its dance beats and Madonna being a new female artist, it only charted on the Billboard Club Play chart, failing to reach the Hot 100 or rock charts. Madonna never really recorded anything like it again after achieving mainstream success with poppier hits. "Burning Up is hard to pigeonhole. This a club record with prominent rock guitar."
